name: Sergei Parfenov
description: Sergei Parfenov is Co-Founder and CTO at Aliwio and Tech Adviser at Symptomato. He builds AI products, learning systems and early-stage software.
summary: Engineering, product and the work in between.
intro: I’ve spent the past decade building products from the ground up — writing software, shaping what gets built, and staying with the messy parts until they work for real people.
homeStory: I joined Yandex Praktikum when it was still a small team. Later, at TripleTen and Nebius Academy, I kept working on the systems around how people learn. At TripleTen, I built AI tools for assessment, search and tutoring. I also co-founded IAWY, an AI tutor that we launched with two bootcamps in Latin America.
homeCurrent: Today I’m Co-Founder and CTO at Aliwio, building software for veterinary clinics. I’m also a Tech Adviser at Symptomato, helping shape a service where AI gathers context before a human health specialist joins the conversation.
blogIntro: I share experiments, technical deep dives and what I learn building AI systems. Nearly 10k subscribers follow my writing.
about: I joined Yandex Praktikum as the 11th member of its early product team. I helped build the product, designed the test architecture for a coding trainer used by 7,000–10,000 students a day, and developed an ML model to assess project submissions before ChatGPT.

At TripleTen, that work expanded into AI assessment, search and tutoring. The problems were concrete: shorten grading time, help students find the right material and make practice easier to produce. I worked from backend architecture through production releases, contributed to learning personalisation and the Mastery Depth Tracker, and helped launch the QA Engineering programme in the US.

As Co-Founder and CPO of IAWY, I took on product direction as well as development. We built an AI tutor with automated project review that integrated into existing learning platforms, and launched it in two bootcamps in Latin America.

Today, I’m applying that mix of product and engineering at Aliwio, where I’m Co-Founder and CTO, building a CRM for independent veterinary clinics. As Tech Adviser at Symptomato, I help shape the technology for a service where AI gathers context before a human health specialist joins the conversation.

collaboration.title: We could work together.
collaboration.description: An AI feature to evaluate, a first product to build, or a system that needs to serve thousands of people. I help teams turn those problems into software they can test and use.
collaboration.approach: We start with a useful outcome and a way to check it. Then we scope a first version, work through the architecture and implementation, and use the results to decide what comes next. I make the technical trade-offs clear in terms of the product, the team and the people using it.
collaboration.invitation: Tell me what you’re building, where you’re stuck and what you need to change.

capabilities.name: An AI idea worth testing
capabilities.description: Choose a narrow problem, define a baseline and build a working prototype. Use the results to decide whether AI improves the product enough to justify further development.

capabilities.name: Building an early product
capabilities.description: Build the first version across architecture, backend and interface. Work with the team to choose what belongs in it, what can wait and what needs to hold up when people start using it.

capabilities.name: Agents you can evaluate
capabilities.description: Define correct behavior, inspect failures in tool use, memory and retrieval, and build evaluations the team can repeat. Check recovery as well as the successful path.

capabilities.name: Smaller models, measured trade-offs
capabilities.description: Test distillation and fine-tuning for a specific task. Compare quality, latency and memory use against a baseline on the same workload, then decide whether a smaller model earns its place.

capabilities.name: Learning platforms & automated assessment
capabilities.description: Build test architecture for coding trainers, ML assessment of project submissions and useful feedback. Connect those systems to the curriculum, where learners get stuck and what practice they need next.

experience.description: Responsible for technical architecture and product engineering, building a CRM for independent veterinary clinics.
Advise on technology for a service that combines AI intake with human support: an AI assistant gathers context before a health specialist joins the conversation.
Built and shipped AI systems for assessment, search and tutoring, connecting backend engineering with the learning experience.
highlights: Designed and implemented a plan and execute assessment system that replaced 140 legacy text-area quizzes. Grading latency fell from 8.4 to 0.6 seconds, a 14× speedup.
Built a CMS vectorization pipeline on Kafka processing 100,000 items a day, and delivered semantic search end to end. Search engagement increased by 9%; time to content fell by 18%.
Automated practice generation, cutting task authoring from 2.5 hours to 18 minutes. Built an internal VS Code plugin that reduced average support time per student issue by 27%.

Worked on Voice Mode for AI Tutor (Dot), integrating WebRTC, speech recognition, an LLM and speech synthesis. Helped bring it to a stable release with 97.8% successful sessions and a median of 1.3 seconds to the first response.

Contributed to learning personalisation and built features that improved student retention. On the Mastery Depth Tracker, I connected product and engineering work to measure learners’ confidence and identify where they needed more practice. Also helped launch the QA Engineering programme in the US.
